rationale: Greek loanword φθονεῖν 'envy, begrudge' with verbalizing prefix ⲣ̄-. The structuring verb of this kephalaion (10× recurrence): Envy/Hyle envies the Ambassador's icon, Adam, the firstborn fathers, Christ's patience, the righteous of Righteousness, Mani, his church, his catechumens. The cognate noun ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'envy' likewise recurs (lines 19, 24).

Greek loanword φθόνος. The cosmic principle of envy as the operative quality of Hyle/Sin. Capitalized 'Envy' would be appropriate when functioning as personified cosmic agent, here paired with ⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲓⲁ 'wickedness' as the dyad of Hyle's malign affect.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉⲓⲱⲣϩ̄ 'look at, watch, behold' (cf. accumulated ⲣⲉϩⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'watcher'). The intervocalic ⲓⲁⲣ for ⲓⲱⲣ shows Lyc. vowel adjustment. Used here of Envy beholding the Ambassador's icon as object of desire-and-imitation.

Greek loanword χαρακτήρ — the technical term for the impressed/engraved mark stamped onto a substrate (coin-die, seal, image). In Manichaean cosmogony of human formation, the χαρακτήρ of the upper icon is what Envy copies onto the fleshly Adam — the imprint/stamp register of the icon-correspondence.

Greek loanword ὑπομονή with Lyc. ⲍ-onset (regular for Greek ὑ-)—the patient endurance of Christ on the cross, a standard topos. Translated 'patience' to maintain semantic-theological connection with the Pauline-monastic register.

Compound: ϣⲁⲣⲡ 'first' + ⲛⲓⲁⲧⲉ 'the Fathers' (in glossary). The 'first fathers' = the apostolic-patriarchal predecessors of Christ in the Manichaean prophet-succession (Sethel, Enoch, Noah, etc.). Standard Manichaean ecclesiological title.

ⲕⲁⲥ/ⲕⲱⲥ 'gall, bitterness, anger' (Crum 121) — distinct from the homograph ⲕⲁⲍ 'land/earth' attested elsewhere in this corpus. Context (Envy 'in her ⲕⲁⲍ within her, after envying me') clearly demands an internal affective state. Lyc. orthography ⲍ for ⲥ/ϩ.

Compound ⲣⲙ̄- ('person of') + ⲙⲏⲛⲉ ('abide, remain'). The constant/steadfast person whose unwavering quality enrages Envy. Coordinated with 'sensible-of-heart,' 'upright,' 'firmly-established' as the marks of the perfected elect.

Greek loan πονηρία (already in glossary as ⲡⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲓⲁ for general usage). Here in Lycopolitan possessed form 'her wickedness' — the doublet-partner of 'her envy' as the comprehensive moral character of the hostile cosmic feminine.
